title: Real-Time Data and File Transfers
keywords: APIs, Asynchronous Operations, and Data Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Real-Time Data and File Transfers in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.

content.intro: This lesson studies Real-Time Data and File Transfers within APIs, Asynchronous Operations, and Data Handling. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Remote data can fail, arrive late, or become stale, so data fetching needs explicit cancellation, retry, and empty-state behavior.

content_blocks.title: Real-Time Data and File Transfers: Asynchronous data workflow
content_blocks.alt_text: Asynchronous data workflow diagram for lesson 87: Real-Time Data and File Transfers. Start the request for the current input → Show pending, success, empty, or failure → Cancel stale work and display useful feedback
content_blocks.caption: Data workflow: model all request states and prevent late or failed responses from silently breaking the interface.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: API integration coordinates asynchronous JavaScript, HTTP requests, server data, loading/error states, and configuration across environments. This lesson focuses on Real-Time Data and File Transfers. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: WebSocket integration
items.text: For WebSocket integration, model pending, success, empty, and failure states. Check HTTP status before treating a response as success, cancel stale work where appropriate, and do not let a late response overwrite newer user intent.

items.title: Receiving live updates
items.text: For Receiving live updates, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Connection recovery and cleanup
items.text: For Connection recovery and cleanup, place DOM or external-system work in the lifecycle phase where the needed element exists, then clean up timers, listeners, observers, or subscriptions when the component no longer needs them. Use nextTick() when code must wait for Vue's queued DOM update.

content_blocks.expected_output: On success, the console prints an array of user objects. Network access or the example service may be unavailable, so failure is explicitly caught.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use in a browser-compatible module or component method. Prefer a local fixture for automated tests and check HTTP status before parsing business data.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Real-Time Data and File Transfers with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Receiving live updates”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Real-Time Data and File Transfers” that applies “WebSocket integration”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “WebSocket integration”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.
